items.title: The Price of Intelligence: A Quality-Adjusted Price Index for AI Services
items.desc: Builds quality-adjusted price indices for the AI inference market from 21,024 posted-price observations across 3,208 models and 86 providers, linked to 4,605 benchmark scores. Matched-model methods used by statistical agencies show prices falling 0.10 log points a year versus 0.73 once quality is adjusted, so 87% of the decline is invisible to current official measurement — and per completed task the buyer's price has stopped falling entirely. [arXiv econ.GN, announced 2026-09-01]

items.title: Tariff Threats, Macroeconomic Expectations, and Policy Communication Strategies: Experiments Based on a Multi-Agent System
items.desc: Turns 300 households from the Michigan Surveys of Consumers into persistent large-language-model agents exposed to social-media information over several simulated months, in order to study how tariff threats shift inflation and macroeconomic expectations before any policy is enacted. The setup lets the authors test policy communication strategies against rapidly changing threat language that conventional surveys cannot track. [arXiv econ.GN, announced 2026-09-01]

items.title: AI and robotics drive an IPO boom in China as Shein lists in Hong Kong
items.desc: Chinese equity markets are seeing a surge of new public listings driven by investor enthusiasm for artificial intelligence and robotics, with Shein's Hong Kong debut among the headline offerings. The piece places the IPO wave alongside other AI-adjacent listings such as humanoid robot maker Unitree's Shanghai debut. [Washington Post, posted 2026-08-31]

items.title: Trump says voters who oppose data centers will 'kill the Golden Goose'
items.desc: Trump publicly criticized the growing bipartisan voter backlash against AI data centers, arguing the opposition threatens the economic engine behind the AI boom. The story frames mounting local resistance as a real constraint on the buildout plans of the largest tech companies heading into the midterms. [Washington Post, posted 2026-08-31]
